findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns the schema resource name instead of client ids and misses per-client resources
findings.body:
`getClientsWithPermission` uses `findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and adds `resource.getName()` for each match.

Two problems follow:
- Per-client resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner)`, which never sets a type. Only the "Clients" all-resource (created in `init` with `setType`) is ever found.
- When an all-clients permission is granted, the returned set contains the string "Clients" rather than any client id.

Callers that use this set to filter or list clients will either see nothing or get a bogus id. Per-client grants are never reflected.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the all-clients resource is missing
findings.body:
`AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource` can return null, for example when the schema is not supported for this resource server or the "Clients" resource was never created. Realms initialized before this PR added the Clients type would have no such resource.

The result is passed straight to `findByResource(server, resource)` and then `resource.getScopes()` without a null check. A permission check would then fail with a NullPointerException (500) instead of returning false.

findings.title: Client removal no longer cleans up V2 per-client FGAP resources/permissions
findings.body:
The removal listener is now gated on the V1 `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature. Nothing replaces it for V2.

When a client that has a per-client resource in the admin-permissions client is deleted, that resource and its scope permissions stay behind as orphans referencing a non-existent client id. They also keep showing up in permission listings.

If both features were enabled at once, `management()` would return `MgmtPermissionsV2`, whose `clients().setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. That would break client deletion.

findings.title: getResourceName not extended for Clients resource type
findings.body:
`getResourceName` only maps the Users type to a human-readable name. For the new Clients type it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`.

Per-client resources are created without a display name, so the admin API and console will show null or a raw internal UUID instead of the clientId. The all-clients resource will not get a friendly label like "All clients" either.

findings.title: Javadoc for void require* methods says 'Returns true'
findings.body: The new Javadoc on `requireView()` (line 96) and `requireViewClientScopes()` (line 101) says "Returns {@code true} if ...". These methods return void. They should say they throw `ForbiddenException` when the corresponding `can*` check returns false.
